title: Autodiag bundler and compressed runbook serializer for ephemeral on-call snapshots
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a compact diagnostics bundler and runbook serializer used for ephemeral on-call snapshots. Improves runbook size, transmission time and desensitizes PII via configurable sanitizers.
description: Motivation: On large incidents operators need compact, self-contained diagnostic bundles that include prioritized traces, contextual runbook fragments, and minimal artifacts suitable for ephemeral snapshot handoffs. Currently the incident-bot attaches raw artifacts which are large and noisy. This PR adds a bundler that heuristically selects high-value artifacts, compresses them, and serializes runbook steps into a compact, human-readable + machine-parsable artifact for handoff and archival. Summary of changes: - New autodiag bundler (incident_bot/diag/bundler.py) implementing artifact scoring and retention tiers - Runbook serializer (incident_bot/runbook/serializer.py) that emits compressed JSONL+gzip blobs and a small index for fast preview - Sanitizer hooks and redaction profiles configurable per-team (incident_bot/sanitizers/*) - CLI & API endpoints to request ephemeral snapshot generation and download (api/handlers/snapshot.py, cli/snapshot.py) - Small additions to tests and fixtures (tests/diag/test_bundler.py, tests/runbook/test_serializer.py) Design notes: The bundler scores artifacts using weighted heuristics: recency, error frequency, stack depth, trace span count, and correlation with alert fingerprints. We keep a small top-K by weight and include a deterministic fallback algorithm so artifacts are reproducible. The serializer produces a compact runbook fragment where each step is scored and can include an optional single-line compressed snippet of logs encoded with gzip+base64. Redaction: sanitizer profiles are implemented as a pipeline of token/regex and KMS-backed secret masking rules; default profile strips known PII patterns but preserves operational context. Rollout plan: 1) Feature behind feature-flag (autodiag.snapshot.enabled) 2) Enable for internal SRE on dev and staging for two weeks 3) Collect perf and size telemetry, iterate heuristics 4) Gradual rollout to all on-call rotations. Checklist: - [x] Core bundler implementation - [x] Serializer format defined and documented - [x] Sanitizer pipeline + default profile - [x] End-to-end e2e tests for snapshot generation - [x] CLI + API integration - [x] Telemetry hooks added (size, generation latency, artifact count) Testing performed: Unit tests added (coverage ~78% on new modules), integration run on staging with synthetic incidents, manual review of redaction outcomes by Security. Backwards compatibility: Existing attachments API still works; snapshots are an opt-in additional artifact. Security considerations: Sanitizers are configurable but default to conservative redaction; shipping snapshots to external channels requires an additional consent flag. Linear/Jira refs: ENG-4821 implements heuristics; ENG-4907 addresses telemetry and rollout gating. Notes: Chose gzip+base64 because many consumers need a single-file artifact and some transport layers strip binary safely; index includes uncompressed metadata for preview. Open questions: - Should we include truncated heap dumps by default or keep on-demand? (currently on-demand) - Do teams prefer md-preview or plain text for runbook fragments? (left configurable)

changelog_entry: Add: ephemeral diagnostic snapshot generator and compressed runbook serializer (feature-flagged). Improves on-call handoffs and reduces artifact surface area.
qa_instructions: Enable feature flag for your team, trigger synthetic incident via tools/dev/sim_alert, then request snapshot via CLI (cli/snapshot.py --team <team-id>). Verify: 1) preview index loads quickly, 2) downloaded blob decompresses to expected JSONL structure, 3) sanitizer removed PII patterns in sample logs.
